name: Autosomal Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for CMT2

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Nerve conduction studies showing normal or mildly reduced conduction velocities with reduced compound muscle action potential amplitudes consistent with axonal neuropathy
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with CMT2 (e.g., MFN2, GARS, NEFL)
Presence of distal sensory loss and foot deformities such as pes cavus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy with electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy and a compatible autosomal dominant family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not always necessary if clinical and electrophysiological criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy of lower limbs
Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes in lower limbs

searchTerms: loss of vibration and position sense

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal upper limb sensory impairment
Hypoesthesia to pinprick in distal extremities
searchTerms: reduced pinprick feeling in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Mild foot deformities other than pes cavus (e.g., hammer toes)
searchTerms: mild foot deformities like hammer toes
foot shape changes other than high arch
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of neuropathy
imaging: Muscle MRI may show distal muscle atrophy
Nerve ultrasound may show normal or mildly enlarged nerves
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MFN2, GARS, NEFL, and other CMT2-associated genes
other: Electrophysiological studies showing axonal neuropathy pattern with normal or mildly reduced nerve conduction velocities

distinguishingFeatures: Demyelinating neuropathy with markedly reduced nerve conduction velocities
Different clinical progression and electrophysiological findings

differentialDiagnoses.diseaseId: hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
Bulbar symptoms such as dysphagia or dysarthria
references: Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009;8(7):654-667.
Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(10):562-571.
